images.title: Common multiples of 3 and 5
images.purpose: Show that numbers in both lists of multiples are the common multiples of 3 and 5.
images.composition: Two large overlapping circles centred on the page with the overlap in the middle, white space around.
images.exact_structure: Two circles of exactly the same size overlapping by about one third. Left circle teal #0072B2 outline, right circle amber #E69F00 outline. Left only holds 3, 6, 9. Right only holds 5, 10, 20. The overlap is filled reddish purple #CC79A7 lightly and holds 15 and 30. Exactly 2 circles, 8 numbers, 3 groups.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any number placed in the wrong region
images.takeaway: Numbers in both lists are the common multiples.
images.description: Two overlapping circles for multiples of 3 and multiples of 5, with 15 and 30 in the overlap.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the overlap and say why 15 and 30 can be in both circles.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
